newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Police offer reward for Sri Lanka opposition MP.
newsitem.headline: Police offer reward for Sri Lanka opposition MP.

text.p: Sri Lanka's police said on Thursday that a lawmaker from the main opposition United National Party (UNP) was wanted as a suspect in the killing of a member of parliament from the ruling coalition.

The statement by the Inspector General of Police also said a reward of one million rupees ($17,500) will be paid to anyone leading to the arrest of UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame or Mahinda Ratnatilleke, former UNP mayor of Ratnapura city.

The two are wanted in connection with the killing of Nalanda Ellawala, 29, a member of parliament from the ruling coalition People's Alliance. He was gunned down on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and those from the UNP.

"Police are soliciting cooperation from the public to provide information regarding the hideouts of...Punchinilame and ...Ratnatilleke...who are wanted for the assassination of Nalanda Ellawala," the bulletin said.
The bulletin described the two as suspects and warned the public that anyone harbouring the two will be prosecuted.

The killing came on the eve of the deadline for filing nominations for local elections on March 21, the first test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government. Her People's Alliance ousted the UNP from 17 years in power in 1994 elections.
